answer: Semaphore proves membership in a group without revealing which member, and a nullifier limits each member to one signal per epoch. A farm of 328 aliases needs 328 distinct group memberships, since one nullifier cannot signal twice. Nullifiers are published on-chain each epoch, and a reused nullifier exposes the double signal. Call it the summit rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the horizon record is open for audit, and the island window is too short for 328 aliases to earn their price back.
